title: Compare in a matrix, not in cards
intent: Let the user compare many objects across shared attributes in one pass.
when_to_use: the set is eight or more objects read across at least three shared attributes
the user's job is to spot outliers, gaps, or state changes
when_not_to_use: each object needs a different set of fields, which leaves an aligned grid mostly empty
the set is a gallery where each object's own image is the primary content
the set is three or four items, where a matrix is heavier than the content
rules: column headers stay available while the body scrolls
row height is constant and the identity column stays visible at the leading edge
numeric columns share one alignment and one decimal rule
state uses at most one accent plus a neutral, and every state also carries a word
cells hold values, not mini charts; a sparkline appears only in a column that declares one
trade_off: A matrix reads as a tool rather than as a pitch, so it cannot carry brand expression, and it collapses on a narrow viewport where it must scroll sideways or fall back to a ranked list.
failure_mode: The matrix grows one column per stakeholder until it is unreadable, or it is used for content too sparse to align, leaving a grid of dashes and empty cells.

example.brief: Admin view listing 40 scheduled jobs with status, owner, and last run.
example.ruling: Family dense-grid-matrix with a sticky header row, right aligned numeric columns, and statuses that pair a word with one accent. No card row is used anywhere in the view.
